# Aligned NORMAL STAR relations: Nov 5 audit

**The user's relation claim is correct in the stated pure scope.** For

```text
S: p.u.*   -> q.v.*
L: p.u.r.* -> q.v.r.*
```

with the same residual r on both endpoints, every concrete pair in L belongs
to S. Choose S's suffix as `r ++ sigma` for each L suffix sigma. The Lean
model proves this for arbitrary finite paths and full mark values, preserving
the opaque complete interface and both bases. It also proves that S union L
has exactly S's concrete relation, that a family of such specializations is
covered, and that reversal of this pure geometry preserves the inclusion.

The model includes an executable exact-prefix applicator and proves equal
results for every exact descendant of L's input prefix. Counted path weights
are additive, so native stored growth is identical:

```text
count(v) > count(u)  iff  count(v ++ r) > count(u ++ r).
```

The same cancellation holds in reverse. No boundary-growth counterexample
exists for this aligned singleton family. The earlier fixed-P MUST example
whose growth flags differ is a different family and does not refute this law.

## No valid finding-loss counterexample found

The search covered the pinned pure AP application, native matching,
normalization, loop observer, C2/C5, handoff and saved replay. It did not find
an end-to-end loss counterexample with equal empty E/mx, the same owner/context/
scope/physical ports, NORMAL STAR/FLOW headers, nonzero nonstatic endpoints,
and identical correlated residual. No project or new native JVM was run.
This is an honest negative search result, not a whole-engine proof of absence.

The previously executed native ancestor case is **not a relation-subsumption
counterexample**. For actual `p.* FLOW NORMAL`, S emits `q.* FLOW NORMAL`,
while L emits `q.r.ANY FLOW DEMAND`. The second result loses suffix
correlation because native matching includes an ancestor/inside input. It
is an operational annotation difference. It does not establish a real flow
present in L but absent from S; concrete L is still included in S.

Unaligned residuals, different E/mx, different interfaces or a changed
premise family are genuine counterexamples to broader rules. They are outside
this selected simple family. They must not be used to reject the aligned
equal-header claim.

## What current code does, and what that proves

* **Matching/application.** `Summary.satisfyingPart` and `insidePart` allow a
  STAR actual above a deeper record premise. `Reference.above` and the typed
  edge applicator lose the correlation and emit ANY/DEMAND. For exact inputs
  below the longer premise the existing native control returns the same
  NORMAL exact output for both rows, as the concrete model predicts.
* **Saved delivery.** `MethodBlockRuntime.offerChild` invokes `replaySaved`
  **before** current child C2 admission. The shorter saved record can therefore
  run on an offered packet even when no current child initial is admitted.
  My Nov 4 generic admission/delivery warning was not established for this
  local saved-replay path. The precision observer's `initials` liveness/C2
  guard is a separate operation, not a gate around saved replay.
* **Parent P and protection.** `LocalRelationApplication` passes the same
  complete parent original to both rows. In this singleton plain FLOW cell
  the record premise mark is abstract; concrete-trigger protection restoration
  in `ApOps.applySummary` has no trigger, and a FlowTree has no TaintTree
  protection mask. No protection counterexample was found in this scope.
  A concrete/ND extension needs a separate law; it cannot be smuggled into
  the pure FLOW claim.
* **C5 and bounds.** C5 checks the same complete parent original against its
  paired entry before restricting the output. For empty E/mx, a shorter STAR
  result above an accepted descendant exit is retained as STAR by
  `restrictConclusionOnly`. It is not rejected merely for being the shorter
  correlated result. It is no deeper than the ancestor-inside long output.
  This source argument supports the positive case; it is not a proof of the
  whole loop-cut/consumer policy for every packed input.
* **C2.** Literal images can differ. An ANY guide at `q.r` emits no initial
  from the above NORMAL STAR `q.*`; it can emit `q.r.ANY DEMAND` from the long
  row's provisional `q.r.ANY`. This follows from the current C2 tail table.
  The difference shows that current admission represents the redundant may
  branch separately. It does not by itself show that deleting L loses a
  concrete source-to-sink flow which S cannot supply.
* **Handoff.** The provisional long output is selected as demand; a singleton
  shorter NORMAL STAR result supplies a record instead. Their literal next
  demand inventories can therefore differ. The next task is to prove this
  guidance dispensable when S is retained, not to claim those inventories
  are already equal. Full entry/exit pairs and the ordinary source/sink seed
  machinery must remain intact.
* **Loop observer.** `LoopObservedFacts` keeps exact pattern/layer/protection
  members; it can distinguish the shorter NORMAL STAR and longer ANY/DEMAND.
  This is a literal-signature difference under the present implementation.
  No complete native example has shown a resulting lost report. A canonical
  relation observer or congruence theorem must justify using a cover quotient
  in the raw/prefix cut test; current exact equality is not that theorem.
* **Effects.** The later-run pure local relation applicator has no rule,
  source, alias or call action callbacks. This nonzero STAR->STAR FLOW cell
  cannot produce ZERO/Reach/Target, and run-1 requests are excluded. There is
  no hidden direct source/Target counterexample within that applicator cell.
  Whole-driver discovery and later concrete instantiation are still outside
  this small model.

## Affirmative sufficient rule and proof boundary

At the **concrete NORMAL relation** level, use this simple canonical rule:
within one complete native interface and compatible headers, retain S and
omit every L obtained by appending exactly the same residual to both STAR
endpoints. Begin with nonzero nonstatic singleton plain FLOW, NORMAL layer,
empty E/mx and the same mode/owner/context/scope/ports. This is a positive
relation antichain rule, not isolated output-fact prefix subsumption. It needs
no GroundingSupport label: native record, actual and complete parent P are
already present at application.

There are two implementation proof levels:

1. **Immediate native-equality subcase:** an offered packet has only exact
   descendant leaves at/below L's premise, with compatible headers and no
   ancestor contribution. The pure applicator results agree. The existing
   one-input native control and universal exact-path model support this
   subcase; packed/native correspondence still needs a focused test/proof.
2. **Full relation canonicalization:** allow the ancestor/inside cell too,
   recognize its extra ANY/DEMAND as correlation loss already covered by S,
   and prove preservation of future concrete instantiation, consumer queries,
   native field cuts and root reports. This is a new explicit relation-level
   discharge/congruence law. No finding-loss counterexample is currently
   known, but that whole-pipeline theorem is not supplied by output geometry.

Restricting same-direction STAR inside matching while retaining it for native
opposite-direction record views may eliminate the redundant provisional cell.
For the covered S/L family that is a plausible implementation route. This
audit does not establish a blanket ban for arbitrary unaligned same-direction
STAR records, MUST actuals or other transfers. That broader matching change
requires its own valid examples and separate proof.

The practical next gates are a pure S/L antichain model connected to native
normalization, exact-descendant and ancestor/packed CEGAR controls through the
actual observer and handoff, then an end-to-end finite source/sink test. A
literal C2/observer difference must be recorded as such; call it a true
subsumption failure only after exhibiting an uncovered concrete relation or
lost real report under the agreed guards.

`StarRelation.lean` proves concrete inclusion and growth only. `check.py`
kernel-checks and audits every public model definition/theorem with one CPU
and a 768 MiB Lean cap. No Classical choice, unproved declaration or native
evaluation is allowed. Existing native artifacts are reused as evidence,
not rerun. No runtime, policy, project configuration or archived receipt is
changed by this audit.

import Std

/-!
Concrete pure NORMAL STAR/FLOW suffix relations. The interface and full mark
are opaque values, preserved exactly. This proves paired relation inclusion,
not a native AP/observer/driver deletion theorem.
-/
namespace StarRelation
set_option autoImplicit false

structure Row (Field : Type) where
  interface : Nat
  inputBase : Nat
  outputBase : Nat
  inputPrefix : List Field
  outputPrefix : List Field

structure Pair (Field : Type) where
  interface : Nat
  inputBase : Nat
  outputBase : Nat
  mark : Nat
  inputPath : List Field
  outputPath : List Field

variable {Field : Type}

def produce (row : Row Field) (mark : Nat) (suffix : List Field) : Pair Field :=
  ⟨row.interface, row.inputBase, row.outputBase, mark,
    row.inputPrefix ++ suffix, row.outputPrefix ++ suffix⟩

def denotes (row : Row Field) (pair : Pair Field) : Prop :=
  ∃ suffix, produce row pair.mark suffix = pair

def specialize (row : Row Field) (residual : List Field) : Row Field :=
  { row with inputPrefix := row.inputPrefix ++ residual,
             outputPrefix := row.outputPrefix ++ residual }

/-- Explicit executable witness: use the same residual on both endpoints. -/
def coveringSuffix (residual suffix : List Field) : List Field := residual ++ suffix

theorem produced_specialization (row : Row Field) (residual suffix : List Field) (mark : Nat) :
    produce (specialize row residual) mark suffix =
      produce row mark (coveringSuffix residual suffix) := by
  simp [produce, specialize, coveringSuffix, List.append_assoc]

theorem specialization_subrelation (row : Row Field) (residual : List Field) (pair : Pair Field)
    (member : denotes (specialize row residual) pair) : denotes row pair := by
  obtain ⟨suffix, same⟩ := member
  exact ⟨coveringSuffix residual suffix, (produced_specialization row residual suffix pair.mark).symm.trans same⟩

theorem union_specialization_is_short (row : Row Field) (residual : List Field) (pair : Pair Field) :
    (denotes row pair ∨ denotes (specialize row residual) pair) ↔ denotes row pair := by
  constructor
  · intro member
    rcases member with short | long
    · exact short
    · exact specialization_subrelation row residual pair long
  · exact Or.inl

theorem every_specialization_is_covered (row : Row Field) (residuals : List (List Field))
    (pair : Pair Field) (member : ∃ residual ∈ residuals, denotes (specialize row residual) pair) :
    denotes row pair := by
  obtain ⟨residual, _, long⟩ := member
  exact specialization_subrelation row residual pair long

theorem empty_specialization (row : Row Field) : specialize row [] = row := by
  cases row
  simp [specialize]

theorem specialize_twice (row : Row Field) (left right : List Field) :
    specialize (specialize row left) right = specialize row (left ++ right) := by
  simp [specialize, List.append_assoc]

def reverseGeometry (row : Row Field) : Row Field :=
  { row with inputBase := row.outputBase, outputBase := row.inputBase,
             inputPrefix := row.outputPrefix, outputPrefix := row.inputPrefix }

theorem reverse_geometry_specializes (row : Row Field) (residual : List Field) :
    reverseGeometry (specialize row residual) = specialize (reverseGeometry row) residual := rfl

theorem reverse_specialization_subrelation (row : Row Field) (residual : List Field)
    (pair : Pair Field) (member : denotes (reverseGeometry (specialize row residual)) pair) :
    denotes (reverseGeometry row) pair := by
  exact specialization_subrelation (reverseGeometry row) residual pair member

def counted (weight : Field → Nat) : List Field → Nat
  | [] => 0
  | head :: tail => weight head + counted weight tail

theorem counted_append (weight : Field → Nat) (left right : List Field) :
    counted weight (left ++ right) = counted weight left + counted weight right := by
  induction left with
  | nil => simp [counted]
  | cons head tail ih => simp [counted, ih, Nat.add_assoc]

def grows (weight : Field → Nat) (row : Row Field) : Prop :=
  counted weight row.inputPrefix < counted weight row.outputPrefix

theorem specialization_growth_iff (weight : Field → Nat) (row : Row Field) (residual : List Field) :
    grows weight (specialize row residual) ↔ grows weight row := by
  simp only [grows, specialize, counted_append]
  exact Nat.add_lt_add_iff_right

theorem reverse_specialization_growth_iff (weight : Field → Nat) (row : Row Field)
    (residual : List Field) :
    grows weight (reverseGeometry (specialize row residual)) ↔ grows weight (reverseGeometry row) := by
  exact specialization_growth_iff weight (reverseGeometry row) residual

def strip [DecidableEq Field] : List Field → List Field → Option (List Field)
  | [], path => some path
  | _ :: _, [] => none
  | head :: requested, first :: path => if head = first then strip requested path else none

def applyExact [DecidableEq Field] (row : Row Field) (path : List Field) : Option (List Field) :=
  (strip row.inputPrefix path).map (fun suffix => row.outputPrefix ++ suffix)

theorem strip_append [DecidableEq Field] (requested suffix : List Field) :
    strip requested (requested ++ suffix) = some suffix := by
  induction requested with
  | nil => rfl
  | cons head tail ih => simp [strip, ih]

theorem exact_descendant_applications_equal [DecidableEq Field] (row : Row Field)
    (residual suffix : List Field) :
    applyExact (specialize row residual) ((row.inputPrefix ++ residual) ++ suffix) =
      applyExact row ((row.inputPrefix ++ residual) ++ suffix) := by
  change (strip (row.inputPrefix ++ residual) ((row.inputPrefix ++ residual) ++ suffix)).map
      (fun rest => (row.outputPrefix ++ residual) ++ rest) =
    (strip row.inputPrefix ((row.inputPrefix ++ residual) ++ suffix)).map
      (fun rest => row.outputPrefix ++ rest)
  rw [strip_append, List.append_assoc, strip_append]
  simp [List.append_assoc]

theorem exact_descendant_result [DecidableEq Field] (row : Row Field)
    (residual suffix : List Field) :
    applyExact (specialize row residual) ((row.inputPrefix ++ residual) ++ suffix) =
      some ((row.outputPrefix ++ residual) ++ suffix) := by
  change (strip (row.inputPrefix ++ residual) ((row.inputPrefix ++ residual) ++ suffix)).map
      (fun rest => (row.outputPrefix ++ residual) ++ rest) =
    some ((row.outputPrefix ++ residual) ++ suffix)
  rw [strip_append]
  rfl

def identityRow : Row Nat := ⟨7, 1, 2, [], []⟩
def wrongResidualRow : Row Nat := ⟨7, 1, 2, [10], []⟩

theorem aligned_example :
    applyExact (specialize identityRow [10]) [10, 20] = some [10, 20] ∧
    applyExact identityRow [10, 20] = some [10, 20] := by decide

theorem unaligned_example_changes_result :
    applyExact wrongResidualRow [10, 20] = some [20] ∧
    applyExact identityRow [10, 20] = some [10, 20] := by decide

theorem pair_metadata_preserved (row : Row Field) (residual suffix : List Field) (mark : Nat) :
    (produce (specialize row residual) mark suffix).interface = row.interface ∧
    (produce (specialize row residual) mark suffix).inputBase = row.inputBase ∧
    (produce (specialize row residual) mark suffix).outputBase = row.outputBase ∧
    (produce (specialize row residual) mark suffix).mark = mark := ⟨rfl, rfl, rfl, rfl⟩

end StarRelation
